name: Question 6
problem:
From top to bottom, fill in the blanks and hence complete the proof of the following statement using the axioms $[\text{A}1]-[\text{A}8]$ given below.

*Given any $x\in V$, if $w$ is a vector such that $x+w=0$, then $w=-x$* 

*Proof:*

$$
\begin{aligned}x+w & =0 &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (x+w)+(-x) & =0+(-x) &  & [\,\text{add }-x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =(-x)+0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A1}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom A3}\,] \\ w+(x+(-x)) & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,] \\ w+0 & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ w & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,]\end{aligned}
$$

The axioms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{[A1]}:x+y=y+x & \text{[A5]}:1\cdot x=x \\ \text{[A2]}:(x+y)+z=x+(y+z) & \text{[A6]}:\alpha (\beta x)=(\alpha \beta )x \\ \text{[A3]}:x+0=x & \text{[A7]}:(\alpha +\beta )x=\alpha x+\beta x \\ \text{[A4]}:x+(-x)=0 & \text{[A8]}:\alpha (x+y)=\alpha x+\alpha y\end{aligned}
$$

Given any x∈V, if w is a vector such that x+w=0, then w=−x

Proof: x+w=0[given](x+w)+(−x)=0+(−x)[add −x to both sides](w+x)+(−x)=(−x)+0[axiom A1](w+x)+(−x)=−x[axiom A3]w+(x+(−x))=−x[axiom __]w+0=−x[axiom A4]w=−x[axiom __]

The axioms: [A1]:x+y=y+x[A5]:1⋅x=x[A2]:(x+y)+z=x+(y+z)[A6]:α(βx)=(αβ)x[A3]:x+0=x[A7]:(α+β)x=αx+βx[A4]:x+(−x)=0[A8]:α(x+y)=αx+αy
